Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
Greets. I have results for only 3 of the 4 events since I came back
early 'cause I have to work (or should I say "be at my desk") today.

The first constructed event had only about 25 or so players. Curiously
small by recent measures. The finalists were Niki Stewart, John
"Giovanni" Knowles, Paul Johnson, Alex Harmon, and David Tatu. Seating
was clockwise like this:

Niki * Dan * John * David * Paul

Very exciting last 10 minutes of this final. Niki was near death and
John was nearer. Alex was going to take down John but Paul had a
Golconda to give John a bunch of pool from. But, Paul knew John had a
Life Boon and he was afraid that John would play the Life Boon to save
Niki. With little pool John couldn't effectively do that so Paul was
reluctant to give play the Golconda on John. They worked out a deal
and Paul played the Golconda. Alex, obviously unhappy with the
arrangement, played a Sudden Reversal. Fortunately for John, in the
first moments of the game he called a Rumors of Gehenna and gave the
benefit to "everyone but Alex". With his second Master Phase Action,
Paul played a *second* Golconda on John, putting John's pool out of
reach of Alex's final assault. So, with moments remaining, Paul
launched his assault on the top-seeded Niki. Paul got her down low
and needed one more turn. Niki drew into the wakes she needed to
live. Tatu made a last ditch effort to oust Paul which came up just a
pool shy. IIRC. Niki had 1 untapped minion--as did Paul. I saw a
Govern and Day Op in his hand and was sure he'd throw them down ASAP
since there were only *seconds* to go in the game. But *HE DIDN'T*
play them!!! He played a Rapid Heal to get a second minion from
Torpor. He played the first Day Op'd Govern and Niki deflected it to
Alex. As it turned out, Paul was correct in his guess that Niki would
have a deflection and his Rapid Heal was much more necessary than it
looked to me at the time. Paul went to do his second action when time
ran out. Wow. Niki won from prior round seeding.

Second tournament (>30 players?) had Ben Peal and Stuart Smith and
youngster Brian McGreal (his first final), and uh, Alex Harmon and
another person fighting it out. I didn't watch the whole thing.
Stuart got two quick VPs then fell to Brian. Ben eventually got
through Brian's massive pool gain but Stuart had the better prior
round seeding with his small cap-presence bleed/anarch deck and took
first place.

The storyline tournament had 38 players, including about 6 I had never
met before. We were even visited by the infamous Semsith himself
(pics soon to be on the vtesinla.org website). It seems he took time
out from his busy schedule messing with Baltimore kindred and
preparing for his annual delivery of xmas gifts to children around the
world. Several players came in costume and that added a lot to the
event.

The most highly represented clans were the Lasombra (6), Brujah (5),
and Nosf. (4). All Cam and Sabbat clans were represented save for the
Brujah-Anti and Gangrel-Anti. Keith Thompson played an Ally-only
(using Wendel to start the process) deck (thought the crypt was
Tremere-Anti).

Semsith first meddled to put newlyweds, David an Robyn Tatu as
Predator and Prey in the second round. And, in a strange
role-reversal for the couple, David was this time the Prey instead of
the Predator. Robyn played Semsith on David and was able to keep it
going for a while. The Lasombra struggled with infighting as 3 of the
6 decks appeared together in the first round.

The finals were odd. Paul Johnson was playing some mean Brujah that
were trying the counter-clockwise rush combat tactic (going backwards
all the way around for 2 VP). He had success with this in the prelim
rounds and was the 2nd highest seed in the finals. He first whacked
Dan Harting who was always just a bit away from launching his Palla
Grande assault on Paul but Paul weakened Dan too much and Dan fell--to
Tatu's benefit. Paul successfully ended Tatu's game as well--to
Szilan Fodor's benefit. Marcos and Szilan and Paul fought for a while
but with time and Paul's library running out it was clear that Paul
couldn't close the deal. Time ended, Szilan won with 1.5 VPs. He
played essentially the same Tremere deck he won the PAcific
Championships (N.A. Qualifier) 2001 with.

Ben Peal actually sat in a visiting judge for the 4th and final event
Sunday night. I don't know how it turned out though. I'm sure we'll
see some additional info later.

Messages.Author: Keith Thompson
Messages.Body:
> Keith Thompson played an Ally-only
> (using Wendel to start the process) deck (thought the crypt was
> Tremere-Anti).

Actually, the ally that serves as the catalyst for the deck is Jake
Washington (Hunter). Since Jake is both a Master Card and an ally, he
can come into play in the Master Phase, and then recruit any ally that
has no specific skill or clan requirement (like a Rafastio Ghoul).

For the LA Storyline Tournament my goal was to not influence any
vampires and play strictly with allies. If I get Jake in my opening
hand, I am golden. In my first Storyline game, I failed to get Jake
and so I died after 45 minutes to a Lasombra vote/bloat deck played by
the incomparable Lasombra himself (Jeff Thompson). Before the game
even started I announced I had no intention of ever bringing out a
vampire provided no one would interfere with my deck (i.e. Sudden
Reversal on Jake). Sadly, I never saw Jake the entire game despite 6
of them and 2 Deal with the Devils. When I finally realized it was
hopeless I influenced to my "best" vampire in my uncontrolled region,
Richard Tauber, only to discover, to my sheer horror, that he has -1
intercept against Lasombra. (Thanks for pointing that out, Jeff!)
Oh, well. I now had 1 hour 15 min to stretch, eat, and wander
aimlessly about the room!

In the second game, I had Jake in my opening hand, and I was going
first, so I knew I didn't have to influence any vampires if I didn't
want to. However, I was a little gun shy from game #1, and I also had
Nephandus (Mage)--the best ally ever, in my opinion--in my opening
hand, so I influenced out Brooke (Tremere Anti-Tribu) and next turn
recruited Nephandus (Mage). Later, I also influenced out Heinrick
Schlempt (Tremere Anti-Tribu) for an extra blocker. I never brought
out any other vampires. (As a point of information, on my fourth turn
I had 6 minions!) Eventually, however, I died to Lasombra stealth
bleed (What?!?, a Lasombra predator again!), but I was quite happy
with Talaq, the Immortal: at the end of the game he had a Gas-Powered
Chainsaw, a Flak Jacket, a Sport Bike, and Mr. Winthrop. Sadly,
though, he was tapped, and I, of course, being an all ally deck (or
nearly so) had no untaps. I also had two Burst of Sunlight in hand,
but that didn't matter much. Also, Nephandus (Mage) #1 had a Sport
Bike and an Ivory Bow, and Nephandus (Mage) #2 had a Flak Jacket and a
Sengir Dagger. Suffice to say, I was very happen with my development
despite 0 VP. I'll work on the deck, trim it down, beef it up, and
play it again. I think the deck can be made into a tournament deck
worthy of the "ALL MASTER CARD DECK", but it needs a massive overhaul.
I may also need to play with more than 6 Memories of Mortality, but
I'll figure it out. At least I tried something different!

As an aside, it is too bad Meddling of Smesith is a vote card because
none of my poor, misunderstood allies could call it.

Keith M. Thompson
Prince of Las Vegas

P.S. Hey, Dan Harting, one of these days I'll get you. And I'll do
it with this deck! You've got some nerve: In response to a
clarification of what "minion" means you said, "What else is there?"
I was mortified. I looked you straight in the face and said very
coldly, "Allies." Someday, Dan, someday . . .

Messages.Author: Keith Thompson
Messages.Body:
> Could you put this in context? I don't remember it.

It was during a pick-up game on Friday night. You were playing your
Followers of Set deck with a Bloodlines guy that kicks ass (white and
red striped background). (Sorry, I don't have Bloodlines committed to
memory yet.) You know: more stealth bleed crap that takes little
skill to put together. ;-) (i.e. sarcasm). You were my predator.

> I am keenly aware of most of the differences between Allies and Vampires -
> for example that Nephandus with Sengir Dagger that you intimidated poor Gary > with deals 0 agg with each dagger strike

OK, you got me there. I forgot that Nephandus has 0 STRENGTH and that
Sengir Dagger requires strength to inflict aggravated damage. Of
course, if you were so "offended" by this you could have pointed this
out to ol' Gary. Still, unless Gary's got Majesty in hand, which he
obviously didn't since he didn't block Nephandus with the "useless"
Sengir Dagger, Nephandus would have shaved off two blood from his
blocking vampire without breaking a sweat. Given enough time, all of
Gary's vampires would be reduced to hunting fools! Sometimes one pool
loss is easier to handle than two blood loss from a vampire.
Situations, Dan, situations . . .

> As for any hostility that you may sense from me: I don't dislike you.
> Maybe I go too far sometimes regarding VTES opponents as enemies;
> maybe our styles conflict.

I wasn't being hostile; I was being sarcastic. Of course, sarcasm is
much harder to convey in writing than in person, so I apologize for
not being clearer with my meanings. However, I do agree with you that
you *often* regard VTES opponents as enemies, sometimes to your own
detriment. I must say dealing with you (in the context of the game)
is like trying to get a rock to do push ups, but as you say, perhaps
it's a style conflict. However, I feel that in "friendly" pick-up
games, you could be more forthcoming and less serious with your fellow
Methuselahs. It is a "friendly" pick-up game, after all. Perhaps a
beer or two would help. Until next time . . .

ORCON 2002 #4 & The deck

After having endured no table wins and VP ties all weekend, I decided
to create and play some Presence crypt machine cheese.

On my first table were :

Me – presence/weenie bleed
Steve Bucy – Kaisid bleed horror
Dennis Lien – Anson/Anarch Revolt
Steven Fazio – Titled vampires that Golconda a lot.
Alex Harmon – Free State Rant/Setites

There were only about 20 minutes of solid play in this round and at
least 45 minutes of negotiation, table rearranging, debate, and some
begging.

The highlight was a deal made where Alex would help Dennis cycle
Delaying Tactics by calling votes to remove Anarchs. Who ever falls
to the Anarchs will set that predator up for a sweep so the
negotiation is pretty heavy.

Alex has just helped Dennis cycle the Delay’s and has two new
actions to take. He chunks in a Charming Lobby and offers to take the
damage from the FreeSR on his own vampires. Fazio expresses concerns
that the second vote will be a restructure and so everyone who can,
votes against. Alex drops a BO and the vote passes. Sure enough, the
second vote that no one can block is a Dramatic upheaval and Alex and
I switch places.

I lost a turn because of the Dramatic Upheaval and am tapped out as
Fazio untaps Arika. I have 10 pool. We all hold our breath waiting
for the unblockable bleed of 90. Arika bleeds. I take it.

He discards!

My turn. All I have to do it discard and let the Anarchs do their
stuff.

What follows is another long discussion about whether Dennis should
life boon Alex now…Or take his chances one on one with me.
Fazio has 6 pool and can survive 4 Anarchs, but we all know Dennis has
2 more in hand. At some point I lost interest in the discussion
because I had nothing to add, nothing to offer and needed to go to the
bathroom. Dennis decides NOT to Life Boon Alex and Alex falls to the
Anarchs, and Bucy falls on his untap. I collect 12 pool.

Dennis takes his turn, drops one more Anarch. Bleeds Fazio for one
– who doesn’t wake ‘er NOTHin’ (!)…..
and secures a VP.

My turn. I have a one TPCounter, one TPMisdirection and 5
friggin’ Majesties.
Yes, Dennis has the edge, but I still had the pool advantage. I opt
to sit there with my little intercept and counter – and wait for
the Anarchs to finish him off.

Next round.

Paul Johnson – Tzi/ Warghoul fighter
Robert Acevedo – True Brujah
Me – cheese
Daniel Walker – Malkavi…..died before we really got a
taste of it.

Paul was not behaving like Paul. Paul did not hold forth. Paul did
not begin a long campaign of ways to bring down the great evil. Paul
did not rush my vamps across the table. Paul began to quietly
influence vamps against a coming no-stealth hoard. A few turns later,
Daniel brings up Lucien. Paul DID attempt to discuss with Daniel how
long he might be able to hold me off. Daniel has deflections. Paul
indicates it might be a good idea if Daniel not deflect to him.
Robert takes great offense to this and displays his displeasure by
grilling Daniel on his intentions. With much bravado, Robert
threatened to come across the table and burn Lucien outright if he
thinks that deflecting to him was an option.

Good times for Daniel.

Daniel said, calmly, that “….he doesn’t respond to
threats” and this, I suppose, was sufficient enough for Robert
to bear his teeth and declare that I had “free reign”.
Me? Awesome!.

Nu the Pillar warped into Lucien and toasted him with 9 ag.

Paul said. “Jesus. How do these Acevedo brothers consistently
get their 4 card combo’s to work? I’ll be lucky to get
off this bleed!”

Daniel died and Paul spent the rest of the game fending off my bleeds
and Roberts bravado.

Robert's Nu deck is pretty great. I spent all week wondering who to
put the TBrujah with in a deck and then here comes Robert Acevedo who
shows us that Nu can take care of things all by himself.

++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

Finals.

Dennis Lien – Anarch/Anson
Me – Cheese
Szilan Fodor – Salubri/Spirit Marionette
Steven Fazio – Titled Vamps who Golconda a lot
Dan Harting – Tor!- bleeder

Having had no control over my destiny in the first two rounds I
actually get an opportunity to make a choice about something that
might effect the outcome:

Sit in front of Dennis’s Anarch Revolts or behind?

Once I saw the field, I chose to sit as his prey and hope his Anarchs
would turbo me thru the table.

The round was quick. Szilan never had a chance to get going but did
get one shot to swipe Lucien from Fazio with a Spirit Marionette, rake
off 10 blood with a Heidelberg, and return Lucien to Fazio much
thinner on blood. Pretty neat. Fazio Golconda’s Lucien.

The bulk of this round was Fazio trying to bargain with Szilan NOT to
Spirit Marionette any more of his minions, should he decide to bring
another one out. Szilan is not making any promises, but only because
he needs to cycle those cards to get to wakes…..perhaps.

At the other end of the table Dennis is calculating his effectiveness
and realizes he is dead on the next pass. He drops another Anarch
(the 5th) – Even after some thought I’m not sure why he
did that. Perhaps he thought I would use all 3 minions to call votes
to get rid of the Anarchs? Perhaps he will explain it to us!!

Dennis falls to Dan Harting. It was only during end game that I had
to actually think about what I was doing, but minion advantage won the
day. I managed to wrest the Troublemaker from Dan and was just about
to contest Lolita with him when he declared it was over.

I noticed that the OrcCon program book had some general rules about
this sort of thing:

"Players may communicate with each other at the board if it is allowed
by the game's rules. A player may never play another player's
position or delay the game by trying to persuade a player to take a
specific action."

delay of game should not have been permitted. Most of the storyline
games I've played have run out time and that's not right. Especially

There is no provision for playing another player's position,
so that is already covered. You can suggest a course or action
("don't bleed him for more than two - he'll bounce it and oust
his prey" or "don't forget the Edge"), but you cannot play
his position (move the pool for the Edge from the blood bank
to his pool, tap his minion and announce a bleed, etc.).

There is already a rule against delaying the game.

To be clear: the "active" player (or the player whose turn it
is to perform some action or to play some effect) is free to
play without waiting for the other players to finish talking
about what he (or anyone else) should or shouldn't do (or
anything else, for that matter).
